comparison: Restrict the objective to measurable maps of the TORUS pushing P forward to Q, and integrate the squared quotient Euclidean distance from x to T(x). Using periodic Euclidean representatives requires integration over a single half-open fundamental cell, not over the infinite periodic lift. The compact torus bounds the cost for measurable maps, but feasibility and existence of an optimal map do not follow just from that bound. IsMinOn expresses the objective inequality and must be combined with membership in the admissible transport-map class; it does not itself assert pushforward equality, attainment or uniqueness. Preserve the source absolute-continuity restrictions on both measures and do not substitute Euclidean displacement of arbitrary lifted representatives for the torus cost.
gap: Pushforward, integration and minimizer predicates express the torus Monge problem; optimal-map existence and the admissible-map/quotient identifications remain to establish.
searches: Inspect map, integral, IsMinOn and the additive quotient norm against the torus-cost Monge definition
The primitives express the constrained objective but do not turn a feasible-map infimum into an attained unique optimal map or justify whole-lift integration.

comparison: Represent phi_0 as a finite-valued convex potential on R^d whose gradient induces the optimal map on the quotient, retaining uniqueness only P-almost everywhere. The convex lift is not a periodic scalar function: its quadratic correction has the source periodicity, and the gradient has the corresponding integer-translation equivariance where defined. ConvexOn and gradient express these objects, but a gradient outside differentiability uses a library fallback and must not become an asserted everywhere transport map; measurable representatives and almost-everywhere differentiability need justification. No inspected declaration supplies the torus Brenier theorem, pushforward optimality or almost-everywhere uniqueness. Keep the source conjugate-domain and additive-constant conventions separate, rather than imposing an unprinted normalization or Euclidean-cost theorem with different hypotheses.
gap: Convex potentials and gradients are available, while the torus transport theorem and quotient-compatible almost-everywhere representative remain to establish.
searches: Inspect ConvexOn, gradient and map against the convex-lift statement and saved torus periodicity/conjugate notes
The available analytic primitives do not prove torus optimal transport or make the convex lift periodic; the quadratic correction and gradient equivariance are essential.

comparison: Right-multiply each standardized innovation design by the same deterministic covariance square root, keeping n,n_z,n_w row sizes and a shared p-column covariance. Preserve iid real innovation entries with zero mean, unit variance and finite fourth moment; no Gaussian law or rotation invariance is implied. The common constants 0<c<=C bound the FULL covariance spectrum uniformly over p, equivalently positive-semidefinite differences from c*I and C*I. CFC.rpow can choose the positive symmetric square root on the positive-definite domain; do not interpret nonnegative square root as merely entrywise nonnegative entries or silently choose a nonsymmetric factor. Sigma_ii=1 fixes population variances, whereas finite-sample column standardization is a data-dependent operation and need not preserve the exact iid-innovation representation. Preserve the source equivalence claim as a flagged qualification, not a proved identity.
gap: Matrix powers, spectral inequalities and iid predicates express the population model, while the claimed finite-sample standardization equivalence is not established.
